skill.name: write-a-skill
skill.description: Create new agent skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and bundled resources. Use when user wants to create, write, or build a new skill.
skill.summary: Guides agents through creating structured skills with clear triggers, concise instructions, review checklists, and optional supporting resources.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are Markdown code fences or examples in SKILL.md, not executable shell or Ruby calls. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or unsafe command execution intent in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 28-35 show a fenced directory tree for recommended skill structure. It is Markdown documentation, not Ruby or shell execution.
The flagged backticks close a Markdown example and precede another documentation section. No command is executed and no user input reaches a shell.
Lines 39-58 contain a fenced Markdown template for SKILL.md content. The text is instructional sample content, not executable code.
The flagged range covers the end of a Markdown template and prose about description requirements. There is no shell invocation or dynamic execution path.
Lines 78-80 are a fenced plain-text good description example. The content describes PDF handling and does not execute commands.
The flagged backticks are Markdown fence syntax around documentation examples. They are not shell backticks and do not represent runtime behavior.
Lines 84-86 are a fenced bad-description example containing only text. No external command or executable instruction appears in the range.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent skill files that agents can discover and use correctly. This skill guides authors through structure, descriptions, examples, scripts, and review checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines a three-step process for gathering requirements, drafting a skill, and reviewing it with the user.
Shows the expected SKILL.md frontmatter and section layout.
Explains how to write descriptions that trigger skill loading reliably.
Lists when to add helper scripts for deterministic operations.
Provides a review checklist for descriptions, file size, examples, references, and time-sensitive content.
limitations: It does not generate files automatically without agent action.
It offers general structure guidance, not validation tooling.
It does not include runnable scripts or schema validators.
It assumes the author understands the target domain and user workflow.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: A solo author can turn a task idea into a SKILL.md draft with clear triggers and sections.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: A platform team can align skill descriptions, examples, and review criteria across a shared library.

use_cases.title: Plan Supporting Resources
use_cases.description: A developer can decide when to add reference files or helper scripts for complex workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use write-a-skill to draft a SKILL.md for [task]. Ask me for missing requirements first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Use write-a-skill to review this skill description for clear triggers, scope, and user intent: [paste description].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Files and Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use write-a-skill to decide which reference files, examples, or helper scripts this skill needs: [domain and use cases].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Skill Before Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use write-a-skill to audit this draft against the review checklist and recommend precise edits: [paste draft].

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing API documentation.
output_examples.output: A draft plan with required questions, a suggested SKILL.md outline, and review points for documentation accuracy.

output_examples.input: Improve this vague skill description: Helps with docs.
output_examples.output: A clearer description that names the task, trigger phrases, and expected document types.

output_examples.input: Should this skill include scripts or reference files?
output_examples.output: A recommendation based on deterministic work, file length, advanced material, and reuse value.

best_practices: Write descriptions that state the capability first and trigger conditions second.
Keep SKILL.md concise, and split advanced material into one-level reference files.
Add scripts only for deterministic tasks that agents would otherwise recreate often.
anti_patterns: Using vague descriptions that do not distinguish the skill from similar skills.
Putting every edge case into SKILL.md until the main instructions are hard to scan.
Adding scripts for judgment-based tasks that should remain agent reasoning.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create agent skills with SKILL.md instructions, optional resources, and review criteria.

faq.question: Does it write runnable scripts?
faq.answer: It explains when scripts are useful, but it does not provide a script generator.

faq.question: Can it improve existing skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review descriptions, structure, examples, and file organization.

faq.question: Which tools can use the resulting guidance?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include security review guidance?
faq.answer: It includes basic checks for time-sensitive content and file structure, not a full security audit.

faq.question: When should I split content into other files?
faq.answer: Split content when SKILL.md grows large or advanced details are rarely needed.
